args.lit: For such a small, rural village, the atmosphere was always busy with at least one boisterous argument erupting after the charged words of a townsperson. This lively arrangement intrigued me, and I decided to investigate further.

While the sights - and smells - of the local civic establishment were certainly an interesting diversion, I could not allow myself to be distracted. I was here to gain insight on the political factions, as I was well-aware that this knowledge could be swung to my advantage.

I was never quite fond of my visits to this place. However, it was ever my duty to make an appearance and my spouse insisted that I would do well to 'mingle' amongst the folk here. So, I made do within the strained situation and struck up a conversation with the first individual that intrigued me.

These spirited events - possible more entertaining to observe than to engage with - took place as the sun set and then sprawled late into the evening. I found myself much more accepted in this environment as the night wore on and inevitably the spirits of all in attendance were roused by the spirits from a local distillery. On this peculiar evening, a few persons caught my eye.
My intrusion was met with jeers and skepticism until I allayed their worries with a clever turn of phrase and charming demeanor.
I was quick to explain to them the merits of dour discretion when royal matters are concerned.
They became especially excited by my presence - commonfolk are so easily distracted - and
After a moment of stunned silence - clearly they were overtaken by my brilliance -
I could see a rift - a shimmering slice in the fabric of time -  open up before me.
After conducting my business, I felt the Earth tremble beneath my feet. My blood vessels pulsed, bulging varicose above my straining muscles as an unseen force seemed to press upon me.
A bolt of lightning carved through the pathway ahead, sending my carriage to an abrupt halt. The air swirled into a violent tornado around me.
My stomach fell. A lump caught in my throat.

We feel the emotional weight of six years of developing this game and writing it all by hand resting on our shoulders. 'They better like it.' A voice whispers. It is the game designer again, self-inserting, which is kind of a hack move.

I think an empty page is exactly what we need right now. Maybe this is a chance to recognize that we're all aimlessly trudging forward through the void. Maybe there's a deeper meaning to it all and we should take a moment to discuss it. Board games just aren't what they used to be. Why do they need electronic apps? Perhaps it's best if we visit the bank and get out of here before the game designer starts acting even more like a hipster.

I could no longer suffer the egotistical competitive nature of my cousins, whose work so paled in comparison to my own. This was my time. This was the era of

args.lit: The fate of the world rested in my hands. It was my discoveries, my ingenious weaponry, my unslakable ambitions that would define this new epoch in human existence. And I put on a demonstration that left no doubt as to whom the glory should be bestowed upon.

Fame meant little to me if it did not carry with it the power to alter the world. I would watch as it transformed - carefully molded by my own hands - into a boundless utopia. My influence could no longer be relegated to the shadows. It was time to claim the Earth for my own and shake it to its very core.

I decided that honor was above all. I would not be bullied into submission by a sycophant searching for recognition. If a duel was required, then a duel we shall have!

The exterior wall near the corner of my estate had been struck by an explosive device. I was immediately suspicious of the clear lines of soot at the base, suggesting that the demolition had in fact been calculated to expose a portion of my laboratory.

The papers within my laboratory were scattered about and a small fire had claimed and blackened a portion of the room. Given the frequency of loud noises and odoriferous ingredients emanating from the room, I was not surprised when none in the house noticed anything amiss.
